source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:2 (Chizkuni; the Great Masorah of parashat Vayeshev; the Ramah's own list)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — the WRITTEN-WITH-YOD law: the feminine pronoun is written הוא throughout the Torah 'except ELEVEN written with yod,' and the Ramah lists them, opening with THIS verse ('Bela — it is Zoar,' 14:2). SNAPSHOT: all eleven of the Ramah's list are yod-written — but SNAPSHOT writes EIGHTEEN yod-pronouns in the Torah (bare היא at exactly 14:2, 26:7, Exod 1:16, Lev 5:11, 11:39, 13:6, 16:31, 21:9 — this row's census — plus prefixed forms at Gen 19:20, 20:5, 38:25, 40:10, Lev 13:10, 13:21, 20:17, 20:18, Num 5:13, 5:14): the Leningrad line spells seven MORE than the Masorah's eleven. A counted-law vs codex split, filed beside the 9:29 death-total war; not merged.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:19 (the seven blessing-verses Masorah)
claim_en: THE HUNDRED WORDS, verse 1 of 7: Gen 9:26 carries 9 words — one of the Torah's seven verses of blessing spoken TO God ('Blessed be the LORD, God of Shem' 9:26; 'blessed be God Most High' 14:20; the servant's two 24:27/48; Jethro's 18:10; the grace-command Deut 8:10; Gad's Deut 33:20). Together: EXACTLY ONE HUNDRED words — 'against the hundred blessings of every day; and seven verses against the seven blessings of Sabbath.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:14 (the Ramah; all books — against the printed Rashi's ktiv note)
claim_en: chanikhav ('his TRAINED MEN' — the Torah hapax the machine holds) written with TWO YODS, one before the final kaf and one after — Minchat Shai: the printed Rashi's 'written chanikho (singular)' is 'an astonishment — no book old or new lacks the yods, and no midrash of the sages reads so'; the Ramah rules two yods. SNAPSHOT: both yods stand — the codex arbitrates a tradition-internal dispute.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:1 (Bavli Chullin 65a; the Ramah; the Meiri)
claim_en: Chedorlaomer — the Talmud (Chullin 65a) transmits the name's writing-rule ('two words — but never split across two lines'); the precise manuscripts, the Ramah and the Meiri: ONE WORD, defective. SNAPSHOT: a single written word at all FIVE Torah occurrences (14:1, 4, 5, 9, 17) — the one-word camp's reading, letter-exact.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:22
claim_en: harimoti ('I have RAISED') — exactly TWO Torah tokens: Abram's oath-hand (14:22 — this machine's own title-word) and Potiphar's wife's raised voice (39:15). The Kitzur: 'she too intended for good, as Abraham intended for the sake of Heaven' — the oath-word's only other holder is the false accusation.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:15
claim_en: le-Damaseq ('to Damascus') — ONE Torah token (14:15, Hovah on Damascus' left); the Masorah's pair: 'I will exile you BEYOND Damascus' (Amos 5:27; edge) — the Kitzur reads the guilt-name (Hovah) as the sin whose exile ran past the same city.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:5
claim_en: u-ve-arba ('and in the fourteenth [year]') VERSE-INITIAL — once in the Torah (14:5, the year the four kings struck); the Masorah's pair: 'in the FOURTEENTH year of king Hezekiah Sennacherib came up' (II Kings 18:13; edge): 'as the nations came against Hezekiah and fell, so they came against Abraham and fell.'

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:18
claim_en: melekh Shalem ('king of Salem') — the two words' INITIAL LETTERS carry שם ('Shem'): 'to tell you this is Shem son of Noah' (the chain's identification rides the letters; the letters themselves are the claim).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:18 (corrected scroll; R. Tam's tikkun; the Sephardic nusach; the printed Masorah; the Ramah undecided)
claim_en: Malki-Tzedek — the name the traditions split over: one written word (a corrected scroll), two words on one line (R. Tam's tikkun), 'written two, read one' (the printed Masorah's tzafnat-paneach class); the Ramah brings both and DOES NOT DECIDE. SNAPSHOT: two word-rows JOINED BY MAQQEF — the two-word camp, joined in breath.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:24 (against the Venice 1560 printing)
claim_en: hem yiqchu chelqam ('let THEM take their portion') — 'so it must be, and not as the Venice 1560 printing has it' (the inverted yiqchu hem). SNAPSHOT: the pronoun stands BEFORE the jussive — the order that seats Abram's demand-word (the machine's third DECLARE) exactly once in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:2 and 14:8
claim_en: Tzevoyim written צביים, read tzvoyim (with vav) — 'the first yod stands in place of the vav of the reading' — at BOTH 14:2 and 14:8; SNAPSHOT encodes written-and-read as TWO ROWS at both sites (the machine's own frozen ktiv/qere accounting, flag 10) — this row locks the bare written form.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:20 (the 'three soft' Masorah)
claim_en: maaser ('tithe') — 'THREE SOFT': the ayin in hataf patach (the compound half-vowel) exactly three times — HERE at the tithe-word's Torah debut (14:20), and Korach's two (Num 18:21, 18:26); every other bare tithe-token points the ayin with silent sheva. Row 1 of 3: the debut.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:20 (the 'three soft' Masorah)
claim_en: The three-soft tithe, row 2: 'to the sons of Levi I have given every tithe' (Num 18:21) — ayin in hataf patach on SNAPSHOT.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:20 (the 'three soft' Masorah)
claim_en: The three-soft tithe, row 3: 'a tithe of the tithe' (Num 18:26) — ayin in hataf patach; and the definite ha-maaser tokens (Num 18:26 twice, Deut 26:12) run soft likewise, 'and every ha-maaser follows it' — probed exact. The tithe born on Abram's spoils carries its softness into the Levites' law.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 14:1
claim_en: va-yehi bi-mei ('and it was in the days of') — the pair stands ONCE in the Torah (14:1); the Masorah's five run through Scripture (Ruth's judges, Esther's Ahasuerus, and the rest — edges): 'wherever it is said, there was WOE in their days' — the war-annal opens with the formula of trouble.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:5 (the Ramah; the Masorah's 'two fully-plene')
claim_en: ha-Eimim ('the Emim') — 'this one alone is FULLY PLENE with two yods; in the Torah there is no other malei-de-malei of this name': SNAPSHOT — the double-yod form once (14:5).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:5 (the same Masorah)
claim_en: ...and the name's other Torah tokens are first-yod DEFECTIVE: ha-Emim at Deut 2:10 (and bare Emim at 2:11) drop the first yod exactly as the rule requires; the second fully-plene of Scripture is Jeremiah 50:38's terror-idols (edge) — the Masorah's own pair.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 14:15
claim_en: aleihem [PASEQ] lailah ('against them — by night') — Minchat Shai rules a paseq (the separator bar) between the words: the night-raid's pause. The words table carries no between-word bar: paseq class, uninstrumented (recurrence).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 44:9; Bereshit Rabbah 43:2
claim_en: THE 318 MEN ARE READ AS ONE MAN, AND THE ARITHMETIC HOLDS. Our 14:14 numbers the trained men as three hundred and eighteen; the chain reads the number as the letter-value of ELIEZER, so that the force was in truth one servant. Computed at derivation: the letters of that name total exactly 318. The reading is reinforced from the same verse's other verb, read as his having EMPTIED the ranks by applying the later exemption rules until only Eliezer remained. Argues middah E29 (numerical value).

check.note: A troop number read as a name's letter-value; the arithmetic computed at derivation and found exact (318).

source: Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:2:12
claim_en: OUR 14:3 IS A MEMBER OF THE THREE-SCROLLS CENSUS. The verse writes the pronoun as הוּא (the written 'he') where the sense requires the feminine, of the Salt Sea - verified in the ink at derivation. The tradition records that three scrolls were found in the Temple court differing in exactly this class of spelling, one carrying nine such written forms and two carrying eleven, and that the majority of two was confirmed and the third annulled. Our verse's token is a member of the eleven. This unit's ink participates in the corpus's own recorded textual-criticism procedure.

check.note: A written-form anomaly verified in the ink, and enrolled as a member of the census by which the tradition records resolving textual variance among Temple scrolls.

source: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Pischa 13:3; Bereshit Rabbah 43:3
claim_en: OUR 14:15's NIGHT AND THE EXODUS MIDNIGHT DEFINE EACH OTHER BY VERBAL ANALOGY. R. Eliezer states the analogy by name - 'night here, night there' - so that just as this verse's division runs until midnight, so does the plague's; the two texts fix each other's timing. The chain reads the division two ways, the night dividing of itself or its Maker dividing it, with the reason given: 'their father acted with Me at midnight, I act for his sons at midnight'. This unit's battle is bound to the Exodus by a named inference rule.

check.note: Two verses in different books fixing each other's timing by a named verbal analogy (middah I2), with the reciprocity stated explicitly.

source: Vayikra Rabbah 25:6; Bereshit Rabbah 43:7; Bereshit Rabbah 56:10
claim_en: THE PRIESTHOOD TRANSFERS ON A WORD-ORDER FAULT IN OUR 14:19. R. Yishmael's baraita: the priesthood was to have emerged from the man who blesses here - but because he blessed Abraham BEFORE he blessed the Omnipresent ('does one bless the servant before the Master?') it was taken from him and given to Abraham. An office changes hands on the ORDER of clauses inside one blessing. The same verse's acquisition-title is disputed - praise of what is His, against the reading that Abraham MADE the Name known and was therefore counted a partner - and the city's own name is derived by combining this verse's element with a later one so that neither righteous man has a complaint.

check.note: An office transferred because of the ORDER of two clauses within a single blessing - a legal consequence read off syntax.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 43:9; Pesikta DeRav Kahana 10:6; Sifrei Devarim 33:4; Sotah 17a:21
claim_en: THE RAISED-HAND CLAUSE OF OUR 14:22 IS PARSED THREE WAYS AND INSTITUTES A TITHE. The verb is read as separation of the priestly portion, as an OATH, and as SONG - three parses recorded. On the first, the census of the patriarchs' tithes opens here: this man separated the great portion, 'and the raising means only the priestly portion'. On the second, our verse is the type-case of adjuring one's own inclination not to act. And the refusal of thread and shoe-strap at 14:23 is priced in commandments granted to his descendants - with the two seats naming DIFFERENT pairs, one giving the fringe and the shoe of release, the other the fringe and the strap of the phylacteries, both carried.

check.note: One verb parsed three ways, instituting a tithe census and an oath type-case; the reward priced differently at two seats, both carried.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 42:2; Bereshit Rabbah 42:8; Niddah 61a:20; Pirkei Avot 6:10
claim_en: THIS BLOCK'S ROSTER IS READ AS A TYPE, AND ITS SURVIVOR'S PROVENANCE IS DISPUTED. R. Avon reads the four kings of our 14:9 as the TYPE of the four later kingdoms - 'as He opened with four kingdoms, so He closes with four' - so the unit's own roster becomes the template of a whole scheme of history. The refugee of 14:13 is identified as Og, but his provenance is disputed between seats: a survivor of this war, or a survivor of the FLOOD - carried dual-track. And a count variance is recorded on our 14:19's acquisition formula, one seat counting five possessions acquired in the world with Abraham among them, others counting four without him.

check.note: A roster read as the type of a later historical scheme; a character's provenance disputed between seats; and a possession-census whose count differs by seat, all carried.

source: Chullin 65a:1-2
claim_en: THE KEDORLAOMER LAYOUT LAW. The king's name may be written as two words but never on two lines — the scribal layout constraint recorded on this unit's own token, against the two-words-two-names premise. Filed F-148, auto-seated (round 36, the name-and-ink block).

source: Chullin 89a:4
claim_en: CONSUMED ROBBERY CANNOT BE RESTORED. Even the perfectly righteous cannot return what was eaten — the restitution boundary drawn at Abram's own save-what-the-lads-have-eaten. Filed F-154, auto-seated (round 37, the table-and-knife block).

source: Nedarim 32b:6-8
claim_en: THE PRIESTHOOD'S TRANSFER. Sought from Shem, given to Abraham at the blessing-order slip, sealed by the pronoun — HE a priest, and his seed not priests. Filed F-168, auto-seated (round 38, the altar-before-Sinai block).
